reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E1 demonstrates coherent nanoprecipitation in a W-based HEA but uses Ni3Ta-based phases, not Cu, and a different processing route. E2 discusses the need for an interlayer but provides no data on Cu doping, nanoprecipitation, or thermal/mechanical properties of such a system. The specific claims about Cu nanoprecipitate formation, conductivity pathways, and property retention are unsupported.
premises: Coherent Cu nanoprecipitates can be formed in a W-based HEA by heat treatment at 700°C
Cu nanoprecipitates will create continuous high thermal conductivity pathways
Coherent interfaces preserve yield strength and ductility
A 20–30% thermal conductivity increase is achievable with 5–10 vol% Cu
The alloy will retain structural integrity at ~800°C under dynamic loading
